relationships.subject: GPR4
relationships.evidence_quote: Mechanistically, the spinal RhoA/YAP signaling pathway was activated by SNI, and this activation was reversed by GPR4 inhibition.

relationships.subject: GPR4
relationships.evidence_quote: SNI-induced mechanical allodynia, cold hyperalgesia, neuronal ferroptosis, and spinal inflammation were attenuated by GPR4 inhibition or knockdown.

relationships.subject: GPR4
relationships.evidence_quote: It is demonstrated that GPR4 regulates neuropathic pain, neuronal ferroptosis, and spinal inflammation via the spinal RhoA/YAP signaling pathway

key_findings: Spinal GPR4 is upregulated after SNI; its inhibition or knockdown attenuates allodynia, neuronal ferroptosis and inflammation.
GPR4 acts through spinal RhoA/YAP signaling; RhoA or YAP activation abolished the benefit of GPR4 inhibition.
